evidence: src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: `if (!isOrderStatus(targetStatus)) { throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status"); }` writes the status check inline.
src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts: `assertOrderStatus(status);` uses the domain's asserting helper for the same check.
src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts and src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts both contain `if (!order) { throw new DomainError("NOT_FOUND", `Order ${orderId} not found`); }`.

src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps product to StockLevelDto inline (`productId: product.id, name: product.name, available: product.availableQuantity, reserved: product.reservedQuantity`), while order DTOs go through toOrderDto in src/application/order-mapper.ts.
src/application/order-dto.ts declares StockLevelDto, a stock concern, next to the order DTOs.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Overall the module is a coherent set of application use cases with shared DTOs and a mapper. But some rules are written in more than one place, and the module's own abstractions are not used consistently.

1. Order-status validation is done two ways. ListOrdersUseCase calls the domain's assertOrderStatus(status). AdvanceOrderUseCase does the same check inline, using isOrderStatus plus its own throw of DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status"). So the error code and message for an invalid status live in this use case and can drift from what assertOrderStatus throws.

2. The "order not found" guard is copied word for word in AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase: `if (!order) throw new DomainError("NOT_FOUND", ...)`. There is no shared helper, such as a repository method that requires the order to exist.

3. Mapping is handled inconsistently. Order entities are turned into DTOs through order-mapper.ts (toOrderDto), but GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline and skips the mapper. StockLevelDto is also declared in order-dto.ts, a file named for orders, which blurs the file boundary.

These are moderate issues rather than unrelated concerns. They still meet the fail criteria for duplicating a rule and bypassing the module's abstractions.

violations.message: Writes the order-status check inline (isOrderStatus plus DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status")) instead of using assertOrderStatus as ListOrdersUseCase does. The status rule now exists in two forms that can drift apart.
Copies the NOT_FOUND guard (`if (!order) throw new DomainError("NOT_FOUND", ...)`) from AdvanceOrderUseCase instead of sharing one load-or-fail path.
Builds StockLevelDto inline instead of using a mapper, unlike the order use cases, which all go through order-mapper.ts.
